subject: Basic Science
page:
The water cycle
The sun heats water in rivers and seas. The water evaporates and rises as vapour.
High in the sky, at about 2 km, the vapour cools and forms clouds.
Rain falls back to the ground. In Lagos, the rainy season lasts about 7 months.
explain: This page explains the water cycle. Heat from the sun turns water in rivers and seas into vapour, which rises. At about 2 km up, the vapour cools and becomes clouds. The water then falls back as rain. The page adds that the rainy season in Lagos lasts about 7 months.
simpler: The sun warms water and it goes up into the sky. At about 2 km it turns into clouds. Then it falls as rain. In Lagos the rains last about 7 months.

subject: Basic Science
page:
The human skeleton
An adult human skeleton has 206 bones. A baby is born with about 300 bones; some join together as the child grows.
The skull protects the brain. The ribs protect the heart and lungs.
The longest bone is the femur, in the thigh.
explain: This page is about the human skeleton. An adult has 206 bones, while a newborn baby has about 300, because some bones join together as a child grows. The skull protects the brain, and the ribs protect the heart and lungs. The femur, in the thigh, is the longest bone.
simpler: Your skeleton is made of bones. Grown-ups have 206 bones. Babies have about 300, and some join as they grow. The skull keeps the brain safe, and the ribs keep the heart and lungs safe. The thigh bone, the femur, is the longest.

subject: Physics
page:
Speed
Speed is the distance moved in a given time. Its unit is metres per second (m/s).
Example: a cyclist rides 120 m in 20 s.
Average speed = total distance ÷ total time.
explain: This page defines speed as the distance something moves in a given time, measured in metres per second. Its example is a cyclist who rides 120 m in 20 s. It gives the formula: average speed is the total distance divided by the total time.
simpler: Speed tells you how far something goes in a certain time, in metres per second. The page shows a cyclist who goes 120 m in 20 s. To find the average speed, you divide the distance by the time.

subject: Social Studies
page:
Nigeria's independence
Nigeria became independent from Britain on 1 October 1960.
It became a republic in 1963.
Abuja replaced Lagos as the capital on 12 December 1991.
explain: This page gives dates in Nigeria's history. Nigeria became independent from Britain on 1 October 1960, and it became a republic in 1963. Abuja took over from Lagos as the capital on 12 December 1991.
simpler: Nigeria became free from British rule on 1 October 1960. It became a republic in 1963. Abuja became the capital, instead of Lagos, on 12 December 1991.

subject: Social Studies
page:
Nigeria's states
Nigeria has 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.
There are 6 geopolitical zones.
Each state has a governor, elected for 4 years.
explain: This page describes how Nigeria is divided. There are 36 states plus the Federal Capital Territory, grouped into 6 geopolitical zones. Every state has a governor, who is elected for 4 years.
simpler: Nigeria has 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory. They are in 6 zones. Each state has a governor, chosen in an election for 4 years.

subject: Chemistry
page:
Melting and boiling points
Pure water melts at 0 °C and boils at 100 °C at sea level.
Ethanol boils at 78 °C.
Impurities raise the boiling point of a liquid.
explain: This page compares melting and boiling points. Pure water melts at 0 °C and boils at 100 °C at sea level, while ethanol boils at 78 °C. It also says that impurities raise a liquid's boiling point.
simpler: Ice turns into water at 0 °C. Water boils at 100 °C at sea level. Ethanol boils at 78 °C. If a liquid is not pure, it boils at a higher temperature.

subject: Biology
page:
The heart
The human heart has 4 chambers: 2 atria and 2 ventricles.
At rest, an adult heart beats about 72 times a minute.
The left ventricle has the thickest wall because it pumps blood to the whole body.
explain: This page describes the heart. It has 4 chambers, made up of 2 atria and 2 ventricles. At rest, an adult heart beats about 72 times a minute. The left ventricle has the thickest wall, because it pumps blood to the whole body.
simpler: The heart has 4 rooms, called chambers: 2 atria and 2 ventricles. When you rest, it beats about 72 times a minute. The left ventricle has a thick wall because it pushes blood all round the body.

subject: Basic Science
page:
Our teeth
Children have 20 milk teeth.
Adults have 32 teeth.
Brush your teeth 2 times a day.
explain: This page is about teeth. Children have 20 milk teeth and adults have 32. It says to brush your teeth 2 times a day.
simpler: Children have 20 milk teeth. Grown-ups have 32 teeth. Brush them 2 times a day.

subject: Basic Science
page:
The solar system
The solar system has 8 planets.
The Earth takes 365 days to go round the sun.
The moon takes about 27 days to go round the Earth.
explain: This page introduces the solar system, which has 8 planets. The Earth takes 365 days to travel round the sun, and the moon takes about 27 days to travel round the Earth.
simpler: There are 8 planets. The Earth goes round the sun in 365 days. The moon goes round the Earth in about 27 days.

subject: Mathematics
page:
Triangles
The angles in a triangle add up to 180°.
An equilateral triangle has 3 equal sides and 3 equal angles.
In a right-angled triangle, one angle is 90°.
explain: This page explains triangles. The angles inside any triangle add up to 180°. An equilateral triangle has 3 equal sides and 3 equal angles, and a right-angled triangle has one angle of 90°.
simpler: The corners of a triangle always add up to 180°. A triangle with 3 equal sides also has 3 equal angles. A right-angled triangle has one corner of 90°.

subject: Mathematics
page:
Percentages
Per cent means 'out of 100'.
25% means 25 out of 100.
To write a fraction as a percentage, multiply by 100.
explain: This page explains percentages. Per cent means out of 100, so 25% means 25 out of 100. To change a fraction into a percentage, you multiply it by 100.
simpler: Per cent means out of 100. So 25% is 25 out of 100. To turn a fraction into a percentage, multiply it by 100.

subject: Mathematics
page:
Exercise: at the market
Tola buys 3 oranges at N50 each.
She pays with a N500 note.
How much change does she get?
explain: This exercise is a word problem about shopping. Tola buys 3 oranges that cost N50 each, and she pays with a N500 note. The question asks how much change she should get back.
simpler: Tola buys 3 oranges. They cost N50 each. She gives the seller a N500 note. The question asks how much change she gets.

subject: Agricultural Science
page:
Growing maize
Plant maize seeds 5 cm deep and 25 cm apart.
Maize needs about 500 mm of rain during its growth.
It is ready to harvest after about 3 months.
explain: This page gives advice on growing maize. Seeds should be planted 5 cm deep and 25 cm apart. Maize needs about 500 mm of rain while it grows, and it is usually ready to harvest after about 3 months.
simpler: Put maize seeds 5 cm into the soil, 25 cm apart. Maize needs about 500 mm of rain. You can harvest it after about 3 months.

subject: Biology
page:
Blood
An adult body holds about 5 litres of blood.
Red blood cells live for about 120 days.
Plasma makes up about 55% of the blood.
explain: This page gives facts about blood. An adult has about 5 litres of blood in the body. Red blood cells live for about 120 days, and plasma, the liquid part, makes up about 55% of the blood.
simpler: Grown-ups have about 5 litres of blood. Red blood cells live about 120 days. The liquid part, plasma, is about 55% of blood.

subject: Physics
page:
Light
Light travels at about 300,000 km per second.
Light from the sun takes about 8 minutes to reach the Earth.
White light can be split into 7 colours.
explain: This page is about light. It travels at about 300,000 km per second, and light from the sun reaches the Earth in about 8 minutes. White light can be split into 7 colours.
simpler: Light is very fast: about 300,000 km per second. Sunlight takes about 8 minutes to get to the Earth. White light is made of 7 colours.

subject: Chemistry
page:
The atom
A carbon atom has 6 protons and 6 neutrons.
An oxygen atom has 8 protons.
The atomic number is the number of protons.
explain: This page explains atoms. A carbon atom has 6 protons and 6 neutrons, and an oxygen atom has 8 protons. The atomic number of an element is its number of protons.
simpler: Carbon atoms have 6 protons and 6 neutrons. Oxygen atoms have 8 protons. The number of protons is called the atomic number.

subject: English
page:
Tenses
The simple present tense describes habits: 'I walk to school.'
The simple past tense describes finished actions: 'I walked to school.'
Exercise 4: Write 5 sentences in the past tense.
explain: This page explains the simple present and the simple past. The simple present describes habits, as in 'I walk to school', and the simple past describes finished actions, as in 'I walked to school'. Exercise 4 asks you to write 5 sentences in the past tense.
simpler: We use the present tense for things we do often: 'I walk to school.' We use the past tense for things that are finished: 'I walked to school.' Exercise 4 asks for 5 sentences in the past tense.

subject: Social Studies
page:
Rivers of Nigeria
The River Niger is about 4,180 km long.
It meets the River Benue at Lokoja.
The Niger flows into the Atlantic Ocean through the Niger Delta.
explain: This page is about Nigeria's rivers. The River Niger is about 4,180 km long. It meets the River Benue at Lokoja, and it reaches the Atlantic Ocean through the Niger Delta.
simpler: The River Niger is about 4,180 km long. It joins the River Benue at Lokoja. Then it flows into the sea through the Niger Delta.

subject: Biology
page:
Digestion
Food stays in the stomach for about 4 hours.
The small intestine is about 6 metres long.
Most water is taken in by the large intestine.
explain: This page describes digestion. Food stays in the stomach for about 4 hours. The small intestine is about 6 metres long, and the large intestine takes in most of the water.
simpler: Food stays in your stomach about 4 hours. The small intestine is about 6 metres long. The large intestine takes in most of the water.

subject: Physics
page:
Electric current
Current is measured in amperes (A) with an ammeter.
In the circuit shown, the battery gives 9 V and the current is 0.5 A.
Voltage = current × resistance.
explain: This page explains electric current, which is measured in amperes with an ammeter. In the circuit shown, the battery gives 9 V and the current is 0.5 A. It also gives the rule that voltage equals current times resistance.
simpler: Current is measured in amperes, using an ammeter. Here the battery gives 9 V and the current is 0.5 A. The page also says voltage is current times resistance.

subject: Health Education
page:
Wash your hands
Wash your hands with soap for 20 seconds.
Wash them before you eat and after you use the toilet.
Dry them with a clean cloth.
explain: This page teaches handwashing. Wash your hands with soap for 20 seconds, before eating and after using the toilet, and dry them with a clean cloth.
simpler: Wash your hands with soap for 20 seconds. Do it before you eat and after the toilet. Dry them with a clean cloth.

subject: Geography
page:
Population
Lagos had about 15 million people in 2020.
Kano is the second largest city.
Nigeria's population grows by about 2.5% each year.
explain: This page is about population. Lagos had about 15 million people in 2020, and Kano is the second largest city. Nigeria's population grows by about 2.5% each year.
simpler: About 15 million people lived in Lagos in 2020. Kano is the second biggest city. Each year Nigeria's population grows by about 2.5%.

subject: Basic Science
page:
Insects
An insect has 6 legs and 3 body parts: the head, the thorax and the abdomen.
Spiders are not insects: they have 8 legs.
A butterfly's life has 4 stages.
explain: This page describes insects. An insect has 6 legs and 3 body parts, the head, thorax and abdomen. Spiders are not insects, because they have 8 legs. A butterfly goes through 4 stages in its life.
simpler: Insects have 6 legs and 3 body parts: head, thorax and abdomen. Spiders have 8 legs, so they are not insects. A butterfly's life has 4 stages.

subject: Mathematics
page:
Area
The area of a rectangle is length × width.
A classroom floor is 8 m long and 6 m wide.
Area is measured in square metres.
explain: This page explains area. The area of a rectangle is its length times its width. Its example is a classroom floor that is 8 m long and 6 m wide. Area is measured in square metres.
simpler: To find the area of a rectangle, multiply the length by the width. A classroom floor here is 8 m long and 6 m wide. We measure area in square metres.

subject: Physics
page:
Sound
Sound travels at about 340 m/s in air.
It travels faster in water, at about 1,500 m/s.
Sound cannot travel through a vacuum.
explain: This page is about sound. In air it travels at about 340 m/s, and in water it is faster, at about 1,500 m/s. Sound cannot travel through a vacuum.
simpler: Sound moves at about 340 m/s in air. In water it is faster: about 1,500 m/s. Sound cannot move through empty space.

subject: Mathematics
page:
Our calendar
A year has 12 months.
A week has 7 days.
February usually has 28 days.
explain: This page is about the calendar. A year has 12 months and a week has 7 days. February usually has 28 days.
simpler: There are 12 months in a year and 7 days in a week. February usually has 28 days.

subject: Agricultural Science
page:
Types of soil
Sandy soil drains water quickly.
Clay soil holds water and can become waterlogged.
Loam is best for most crops; it is about 40% sand, 40% silt and 20% clay.
explain: This page compares soils. Sandy soil drains quickly, while clay soil holds water and can become waterlogged. Loam is best for most crops; it is about 40% sand, 40% silt and 20% clay.
simpler: Water runs through sandy soil fast. Clay soil keeps water in. Loam is the best soil for crops: about 40% sand, 40% silt and 20% clay.

subject: Health Education
page:
Burns
Cool a small burn under clean running water for 20 minutes.
Do not put butter or oil on a burn.
Get help from an adult or a health worker.
explain: This page explains what to do for burns. A small burn should be cooled under clean running water for 20 minutes. Do not put butter or oil on it, and get help from an adult or a health worker.
simpler: Hold a small burn under clean running water for 20 minutes. Never put butter or oil on it. Ask an adult or a health worker for help.

subject: English
page:
Exercise 7: Plurals
Write the plural of these 6 words: child, mouse, tooth, foot, man, woman.
You have 10 minutes.
explain: This is Exercise 7, about plurals. It asks you to write the plural of 6 words: child, mouse, tooth, foot, man and woman. You have 10 minutes.
simpler: Exercise 7 is about plurals. Write the plural of 6 words: child, mouse, tooth, foot, man and woman. You have 10 minutes.

subject: Civic Education
page:
Voting
Nigerians can vote from the age of 18.
Presidential elections hold every 4 years.
Voters need a Permanent Voter Card (PVC).
explain: This page is about voting in Nigeria. Nigerians can vote from the age of 18, and presidential elections are held every 4 years. Voters need a Permanent Voter Card, or PVC.
simpler: In Nigeria you can vote when you are 18. The president is elected every 4 years. To vote you need a Permanent Voter Card.
